name: Resi
shortDescription: A US livestreaming and video platform for churches and organisations, designed around resilient delivery, social distribution and multi-site broadcasting.
suitableContexts: Multi-site teams evaluating a central broadcast workflow

pricing.summary: Resi publishes US-dollar livestreaming plans. Its Social Only plan is shown at US$119 per month on an annual billing basis, and it also offers higher-level live and multi-site options; current UK pricing and eligibility need confirmation.

tiers.label: Social Only
tiers.detail: Published annual-billing price for Facebook and/or YouTube streaming

tiers.label: Enterprise
tiers.detail: Published annual-billing price for a higher-level livestreaming option

support: Seven-day live customer support stated on Social Only plan

editorial.assessment: Resi positions its service around resilience rather than low-cost broadcasting, and its published entry pricing reflects that. It may be relevant where a church has material reliability or multi-site needs, but it is a US product and should be evaluated with the actual venue network and production workflow.
bestFor: Churches where interrupted broadcasts have a real pastoral or operational cost
Multi-site churches assessing central-to-campus video delivery
strengths: Published plan details and Sunday-relevant support statement
limitations: Higher US-dollar starting price than basic streaming approaches
UK availability, hardware and final plan scope need confirmation

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches where interrupted broadcasts have a real pastoral or operational cost
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Higher US-dollar starting price than basic streaming approaches

longForm.verdict: Resi should be compared as a reliability and distribution service, not merely as a way to send a stream to social platforms. Its stronger case is where a disrupted service, a multi-site feed or a demanding online audience makes broadcast continuity worth paying for.

decisionLens.heading: The cost of failure is the useful comparison.
decisionLens.text: For some churches, a basic social stream is sufficient. Others need a clear recovery plan when the internet degrades or a broadcast must reach another site. Define that consequence first, then test the provider’s process, equipment and support response against it.

sections.heading: Resilience, distribution and scale
sections.question: When is a specialist resilient-streaming service worth it?
paragraphs: Resi describes a resilient protocol, monitoring and alerting, social destinations and options for multi-site video distribution. Those are meaningful only when the team has a defined operational risk that a simpler workflow does not address.

A purchase decision should include the entire signal chain: cameras, audio, encoding, venue upload capacity, receiving locations and a fallback communication plan. Request a scope and quote that reflects that real setup.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not assign an independent review score. It uses Resi’s current public pricing and church livestreaming material.
themes: Reliability is a distinct buying criterion from basic social streaming.
A multi-site use case needs end-to-end technical validation.
userFeedback.caveat: The supplier’s reliability statements are product claims; this directory has not independently tested a Resi broadcast or confirmed UK commercial availability.

faq.question: How much does Resi cost?
faq.answer: Resi’s pricing page shows Social Only at US$119 per month on annual billing, with higher options including Enterprise at US$689 per month. Confirm the current quote and scope directly.

faq.question: Does Resi offer a free trial?
faq.answer: A free trial was not confirmed from the material reviewed. Resi does offer a guided demo request.

faq.question: Is Resi for multi-site churches?
faq.answer: Resi publishes multi-site distribution options. A church should confirm the required hardware, destinations, network conditions and plan before treating this as a ready-to-use multi-site solution.
